definitions.explanation: A shop that sells ready-made dishes and side dishes for home consumption. These shops are a common feature of Japanese shopping streets, department store basements, and supermarkets, offering a wide variety of cooked foods from croquettes to simmered vegetables.

examples.japanese: お{惣菜屋|そうざいや}でコロッケを{買|か}った。
examples.english: I bought croquettes at the deli.

examples.japanese: {駅前|えきまえ}のお{惣菜屋|そうざいや}はいつも{混|こ}んでいる。
examples.english: The deli in front of the station is always crowded.

examples.japanese: {仕事|しごと}で{疲|つか}れた{日|ひ}は、お{惣菜屋|そうざいや}で{夕飯|ゆうはん}のおかずを{何品|なんぴん}か{買|か}って{帰|かえ}る。
examples.english: On days when I'm tired from work, I buy a few side dishes from the deli on the way home for dinner.

notes:
The polite prefix お is almost always attached in everyday speech; {惣菜屋|そうざいや} without お sounds somewhat blunt. The word combines {惣菜|そうざい} (side dishes, prepared foods) with {屋|や} (shop, store).

These shops are deeply embedded in Japanese daily life, particularly in {商店街|しょうてんがい} (shopping streets) and the basement food floors ({デパ地下|でぱちか}) of department stores. They cater to busy households and single people who want home-style cooking without cooking themselves.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- お{惣菜屋|そうざいや}で{買|か}う: to buy at a deli
- {町|まち}のお{惣菜屋|そうざいや}: neighborhood deli
- お{惣菜屋|そうざいや}の{弁当|べんとう}: deli bento box

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {惣菜|そうざい}: prepared side dishes — the food itself, not the shop
- {総菜|そうざい}: same word, alternate kanji
- デリ: deli — English loanword, used for Western-style delicatessens
- {弁当屋|べんとうや}: bento shop — specializes in boxed lunches specifically
